title: La Paloma
description: Sebastián Iradier's habanera of about 1863, one of the most recorded songs ever, for 2 to 4 singers, sung in Spanish: the first verse and the refrain, the bass singing the habanera's rhythm on "dm" under the tune. A stretch song: its tune runs a little wider than a beginner's comfortable range, so take the high and low notes gently, or move the key.

licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella on the printed chords
licence.source: La Paloma, canción americana, by Sebastián Yradier, voice and piano (Century Music Publishing Co., New York, edited edition with no named editor, copyright 1906, plate 84-4), pp. 2 to 5, verse 1 and the refrain in C, checked against the same song in Artists' Vocal Album (White, Smith & Co., Boston, 1887), pp. 66 to 69; read from the scans at archive.org/details/lapalomadovecanc00yrad and archive.org/details/artistsvocalalbu00bost
